rules.citation: Chapter 9, Article 8, Division 7 of the San Diego Municipal Code
rules.effective_date_basis: Retitled to “Residential Tenant Protections” on 5-25-2023 by O-21647 N.S.; effective 6-24-2023.
rules.title: Just cause eviction protections and relocation assistance for San Diego tenants
rules.requirement: A landlord may not terminate a covered San Diego tenancy without at-fault or no-fault just cause listed in the ordinance. For no-fault terminations, the landlord must give required written notices and provide relocation assistance equal to two months of actual rent, or three months for a senior or disabled tenant, with additional re-rental and buyout protections in specified circumstances.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; no-fault relocation = 2 months’ actual rent, or 3 months for senior or disabled tenants

coverage.small_owner_exception: Residential rental property, including a mobilehome, that is alienable separate from title to any other dwelling unit is exempt if the landlord is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, and the required written exemption notice is provided.
coverage.other_unresolvable: Excludes transient and tourist hotel occupancy, short-term residential occupancy, deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing except Section 8, mobilehomes subject to the Mobilehome Residency Law, specified institutional/care/nonprofit transitional housing, dormitories, shared-facility rentals with a resident landlord, certain owner-occupied single-family arrangements, and tenancies that do not continuously exceed 30 days or are fixed terms of three months or less including extensions or renewals.
coverage.summary: Applies to San Diego residential rental property tenancies of more than 30 days unless a listed property type, owner-occupied arrangement, newer certificate of occupancy, separate-alienable small-owner property, or other specified circumstance is exempt.

rules.exemptions: This Division does not apply to transient and tourist hotel occupancy; short-term residential occupancy; deed-restricted affordable housing; subsidized affordable housing except Section 8; mobilehomes subject to the Mobilehome Residency Law; specified nonprofit hospital, religious facility, extended care, elderly care, adult residential, or nonprofit transitional housing; dormitories; rentals where the tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with a landlord who maintains a principal residence there; certain owner-occupied single-family residences; an owner-occupied two-unit property; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years unless it is a mobilehome; and separately alienable residential rental property where the landlord is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management and required notice is given.
rules.penalty: A tenant may sue for injunctive relief, equitable relief, money damages, and punitive damages; may raise violations as an affirmative defense; wrongful eviction or attempted recovery in violation of the Division creates liability for not less than three times actual economic damages; failure to provide required relocation assistance creates liability for not less than three times the required relocation assistance and actual economic damages; attorney’s fees and costs may be awarded for material violations; noncompliant termination notices are void; and the City may enforce with civil and criminal remedies.
rules.interaction: The ordinance states its rights are in addition to state or federal rights, and required relocation assistance is credited against any other relocation assistance required by federal, state, or other local law.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
